subject: zoology
question_text: What is the function of radula? Give the name of the group of molluscs which do not possess a radula.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack zoology section (book p.53, VSAQ 95). page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Function of the radula
steps.why: The radula scrapes rather than bites, which is why the molluscs that use it feed on films of algae and not on large pieces of food.
common_mistakes: Calling the radula a tongue. It is a toothed rasping ribbon, not a muscular tongue.
Writing that it grinds food in the stomach. It works at the mouth, in the buccal cavity.
steps.memory_tip: Radula rasps: a ribbon of teeth that scrapes food off a surface.
steps.margin_note: Say what it is and what it does. Two or three lines.
lines: The radula is a ribbon of chitinous teeth in
the buccal cavity of most molluscs.
It is a rasping organ used for feeding.
It scrapes food off a surface and carries the
scraped particles back into the gut.

steps.label: The group without a radula
steps.why: The radula scrapes and the gill strains, so the animal that filters its food is the one that does without a radula.
common_mistakes: Naming Gastropoda. Snails have a well developed radula; it is the bivalves that lack one.
Writing 'oysters'. Name the class: Bivalvia or Pelecypoda.
steps.memory_tip: Bivalves filter with their gills, so they need no rasping ribbon.
steps.margin_note: Name the class, then one line on why it does without a radula.

lines.text: Radula is absent in class Bivalvia

lines: The radula is absent in the class Bivalvia,
Bivalves are filter feeders. They strain food

insider_note: Write both names for the class, Bivalvia and Pelecypoda, because different question papers have used each of them.
